reviews.text:
I have no choice but to go here because it's the only place within a reasonable distance.

The receptionist suddenly starts using informal language or doesn't respond at all, which makes paying very unpleasant.
This is an ophthalmology clinic specializing in animals. They provide very detailed explanations. It's a short walk from the station (there is no parking available).

I think the vet is good.
However, even if the cost of the exam is unavoidable, the cost of the eye drops is quite high (about three times what you would pay at a regular hospital).
Also, there are few specialized ophthalmology hospitals, so I have to travel a long way to go there, but there's no parking, so it's difficult to travel with my pet. I often have to cancel appointments, especially on rainy days.

We received excellent care for juvenile cataracts, retinal detachment, and glaucoma.

He is a truly trustworthy doctor.

Before the surgery, our pet's eye pressure was high, so surgery couldn't be performed for a while. We waited until it stabilized with eye drops.

When surgery was possible, he said, "We'll do our best with the surgery, but the most important thing is that you, the owner, continue to provide lifelong care, including eye drops, after the surgery!" I will never forget those words.

At another hospital we visited for an examination before coming to this one, they said some insensitive things.

I'm so glad we found Dr. Kobayashi.

There may be various opinions, but we were able to openly discuss everything, including the examination results from the other hospital, and he listened attentively.

I think it's best to first express your feelings about your concerns and what kind of treatment you want.

When we moved to another prefecture and told him we would still come for regular checkups, he introduced us to an ophthalmologist closer to our new location, saying it would be better to have someone who can see our pet immediately if something happened, and he also shared the data with us.

Thanks to everyone's support, I'm still healthy and well five years later.

The head doctor and the staff in the examination rooms were very pleasant. However, the receptionist seemed overwhelmed and dismissive, which was disappointing.

While I appreciate the availability of private rooms, some patients leave their belongings and reserve seats while they are away from their appointments, making it impossible to use them. Furthermore, it's difficult to tell if a room is occupied without peeking, which is unpleasant for both those peeking and those being peeked at. I would appreciate it if this could be improved.
